documented_behavior: android.webkit.WebView.addJavascriptInterface(Object, String) injects the supplied object under the supplied JavaScript name.
Android documents that the injected object is available to all frames of the page, including iframes.

For applications targeting API level 17 or later, JavaScript can access public methods annotated with android.webkit.JavascriptInterface; older target/device combinations have broader legacy exposure behavior.
Injected objects become visible to JavaScript on the next page load or reload.

Android documents that addJavascriptInterface lacks origin-based access control: the app cannot safely determine the calling frame's URL or origin, and WebView.getUrl() is not a security-valid caller check.
JavaScript-to-Java bridge calls occur on a WebView background thread, requiring application-side thread-safety handling.
preconditions: The application calls WebView.addJavascriptInterface with a non-null object and non-null bridge name.
JavaScript is enabled before the injected object is expected to be used.
A subsequent page load or reload makes the object visible to page JavaScript.
The bridge method is exposed under the applicable Android target-SDK and device-version rules, normally as a public @JavascriptInterface method for modern target SDKs.
JavaScript executing in a loaded WebView frame invokes the injected object name and method.

events.condition: Observing addJavascriptInterface(...) or the alias literal establishes only a possible registration site. The predicate requires that an ElementPickerBridge instance is passed to android.webkit.WebView.addJavascriptInterface with the name "blockadsPickerProxy", that JavaScript is enabled, and that a page is subsequently loaded or reloaded so the injected object becomes visible.
events.name: javascript_bridge_registered

events.condition: Observing the method declaration or annotation establishes only that a candidate entry point exists. The predicate requires that onPickerCompleted is public and JavaScript-exposed under the app's target-SDK/device compatibility conditions, and that JavaScript in a loaded frame invokes the registered alias. Android documents that addJavascriptInterface exposes the object to every frame, including iframes, and does not provide origin-based caller identification.
events.name: bridge_method_exposed_to_web_content

events.condition: Observing a call to onPickerCompleted or construction/use of ElementRule does not prove persistence or attacker control. The predicate requires interprocedural data flow from the JavaScript-supplied cssSelector and domain parameters into a stored ElementRule, with domain retained as the rule's effective target and with no effective user-confirmation, authorization, origin-validation, or same-domain binding on that path.
events.name: page_arguments_reach_rule_persistence

events.condition: A persisted rule alone is insufficient. The predicate requires that a page-controlled domain argument can designate a domain different from the currently loaded page, that the rule survives the current page/session as claimed, and that later rule application uses that stored domain and selector to hide content for the designated domain.
events.name: cross_domain_persistent_effect

important_note: WebViewJavascriptBridgeSpec is a detector concern, not a published Android, CrySL, or library API type. The authoritative Android sources verify the WebView JavaScript-bridge semantics only. They do not independently verify the reported application's ElementPickerBridge implementation, its BrowserViewModel persistence flow, user-interface behavior, supported SDK configuration, or runtime exploitability. The supplied finding is explicitly a static candidate and not evidence of execution.
forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: Do not infer that a type named WebViewJavascriptBridgeSpec exists in Android, CrySL, a detector catalog, or the application.

Do not infer that app.pwhs.blockads.ui.browser.picker.ElementPickerBridge is annotated with @JavascriptInterface, public, or registered through addJavascriptInterface without inspecting the relevant application artifact or source.
Do not infer that JavaScript is enabled merely because a WebView bridge registration site exists.
Do not infer that every visited top-level site can invoke the method solely from the registration alias; page loading, JavaScript execution, method exposure, and bridge reachability remain necessary.

Do not infer that the calling frame is the top-level page, trusted, or same-origin; Android documents that injected objects are available to all frames and that the app cannot determine the calling frame's origin.
Do not infer that the domain parameter is attacker-controlled, used unchanged, cross-domain, or persisted durably without data-flow and storage evidence.

Do not infer absence of confirmation from absence of a confirmation call in the bridge method alone; confirmation or authorization may occur in callers, ViewModel code, repository code, or UI state handling.
Do not infer a runtime CWE-749 vulnerability, impact, or exploitability from this static candidate alone.

name: WebViewJavascriptBridgeSpec
source_title: Native API access JavaScript bridge | Android Developers
semantic_scope: The concern models an Android WebView JavaScript bridge whose reported application-specific callback, ElementPickerBridge.onPickerCompleted(cssSelector, domain), may accept strings from web content and may feed them into persistent element-hiding rules. Its platform scope is android.webkit.WebView.addJavascriptInterface(Object, String) and android.webkit.JavascriptInterface; its application-specific persistence claim is limited to the supplied detector finding.
known_false_positive_shapes: The alias is registered only on a WebView that loads application-authored, non-navigable content, despite a broad-looking registration site.
The bridge is registered transiently and removed or replaced before untrusted content or non-picker pages can load.
onPickerCompleted is not publicly JavaScript-accessible under the application's target-SDK/device combination, or JavaScript is disabled.
The page cannot invoke the callback because the alias is unavailable until a reload that does not occur on the relevant path.
The callback ignores supplied domain values, derives the effective domain from a trusted source, or rejects a value that differs from a validated current domain.
ElementRule creation is in-memory, scoped to a current picker session, or discarded before subsequent pages can consume it.
An effective user confirmation, authorization requirement, or picker-active-state check exists outside the locally matched method body.
Stored rules are never applied to the reported target domain, or selector execution is constrained so that no meaningful content-hiding effect occurs.
protocol: WebView.addJavascriptInterface(ElementPickerBridge, "blockadsPickerProxy") -> page or iframe JavaScript invokes blockadsPickerProxy.onPickerCompleted(cssSelector, domain) after a page reload -> bridge receives page-controlled strings -> [detector-reported static flow] BrowserViewModel persists an ElementRule using cssSelector and domain.

detector_examples.message: Static candidate (not executed): the in-app browser registers ElementPickerBridge as 'blockadsPickerProxy' on every page it loads, not only while the element picker is active, and onPickerCompleted(cssSelector, domain) is persisted by BrowserViewModel as an ElementRule for the page-supplied domain without user confirmation, so any visited website can plant persistent hiding rules for other domains (CWE-749).
